sentences.text: Hyposaurus is an extinct marine crocodyliform belonging to the family Dyrosauridae, classified as a mesosuchian crocodyliform.
The genus name Hyposaurus refers to a unique hypapophyseal keel extending on the ventral surface of the vertebrae.
This animal had a long tail, eyes positioned on the sides of its head, and a long snout with many uniform teeth.

Hyposaurus differs from Teleosaurus by having teeth with a more robust size and vertical orientation, and it differs from modern crocodiles by having tall neural spines, vertically oriented ribs, and keel-less osteoderms.
The dorsal shield of Hyposaurus consists of at least 12 horizontal rows of paravertebral and accessory osteoderms arranged in four columns: two paravertebral and two lateral.
Hyposaurus is closely related to the genera Dyrosaurus and Congosaurus.
Specialized osteoderms suggest Hyposaurus had a trunk bracing system that allowed low-mass individuals to high-walk or gallop.
Hyposaurus rogersii is a contender for the second smallest species in the family Dyrosauridae.
The genus Hyposaurus was first described by Richard Owen in 1849.

The first fossil recognized by Owen in 1849 consisted of two amphicoelous vertebrae discovered by Professor Henry Roger in the greensand beds of New Jersey, now the location of the Edelman Fossil Park and Museum.
Edward Drinker Cope found a second fossil in Brazil in 1886, which included a lower jaw, vertebrae, and various other bones.
Schwarz and colleagues described new postcranial skeletons of Hyposaurus in 2006, focusing primarily on the vertebrae.
Hyposaurus lived in shallow, near-shore marine environments and possessed many aquatic adaptations.
Short transverse processes on the tail vertebrae imply that Hyposaurus did not move its tail vertically and was likely not a diving animal.
The weakly amphicoelous nature of Hyposaurus vertebrae indicates both sides of the centrum are concave.

Hastings and colleagues used mandibular and cranial characteristics to map a new dyrosaurid skull from Colombia onto a cladogram including Hyposaurus, and analysis suggests Dyrosauridae originated in Africa and dispersed to South America in the Late Cretaceous or very early Paleocene.
A Sudanese fossil was identified as Hyposaurus based on its flat mandible and elliptical mandibular symphysis.
The phylogeny of Hyposaurus is disputed, with some researchers suggesting it is a sister taxon to Dyrosaurids, Congosaurus, and Acherontisuchus.
In 2007, Stéphane Jouve considered Sokotosaurus and Wurnosaurus as doubtful genera indistinguishable from each other and North American forms.
Six species are currently recognized within the genus Hyposaurus: H. derbianus, H. natator, H. nopcsai, H. paucidens, H. rogersii, and H. wilsoni.
Hyposaurus lived from the Maastrichtian to the Thanetian, approximately 72.2 to 56 million years ago.

Fossils of Hyposaurus have been found in the Paleocene Maria Farinha Formation in Brazil, the Iullemmeden Basin in West Africa, and Maastrichtian strata in New Jersey, USA. The type species H. rogersii was described by Richard Owen in 1849 based on Late Cretaceous fossils from North America. Edward Drinker Cope described the species H. derbianus in 1886 based on fossils found in Brazil. Swinton described two species from Paleocene deposits in Nigeria in 1930, classifying them as the genera Sokotosaurus and Wurnosaurus.
It is debated whether H. wilsoni and H. nopcsai are distinct species, as their little variation suggests one might be a nomen dubium despite fossil evidence for two.
